The diagram shown above is the slope field for which of the following differential equations?
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14045300/assets/2e9bd658eb426a7e2d5869f2fd9499e846ab82f25edcef6dc5c6f42e38b188bd.png)

 

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the lines $x=-1$ and $y=0,$ as shown above. Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on both of these lines. 

Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =xy+y=(x+1)y \\ {y}^{′} & =(x+1)^{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, the lines $x=-1$ and $y=0$ divide the plane into $4$ regions. The sign of the slopes in each of the $4$ regions are easily deduced by considering the behavior of the solution curves in these regions. This information is summarized in the following table:

| $y>0$ | $↘$

$(-)$ | $↗$

$(+)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ | $↗$

$(+)$ | $↘$

$(-)$ |
|  | $x<-1$ | $x>-1$ |

 
Of the remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}=xy+y=(x+1)y.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is ${y}^{′}=xy+y.$
